beans.title: Bean guide
beans.intro: Coffee species, processing and roast level all change the right water temperature. Pick your beans' roast level.
beans.roast.label: Roast level
beans.roast.lightHint: Dense beans that are harder to extract, so use hotter water.
beans.roast.mediumHint: Balanced. Start in the middle, then adjust to taste.
beans.roast.darkHint: Brittle beans that turn bitter easily, so go cooler.
beans.arabica.desc: Grown at high altitude. The go-to coffee for manual brewing.
beans.arabica.flavor: Bright acidity, sweet, fruity or floral aroma
beans.robusta.desc: Nearly twice the caffeine of arabica. Great for espresso, milk coffee and tubruk.
beans.robusta.flavor: Bold bitterness, chocolate, nutty, heavy body
beans.liberica.desc: Large, uneven beans, mostly from Jambi and Kalimantan.
beans.liberica.flavor: Jackfruit aroma, smoky, a little woody
beans.washed.desc: Skin and fruit mucilage are washed off before drying.
beans.natural.desc: Whole coffee cherries are dried with the skin on.
beans.honey.desc: Skin removed, some mucilage left on while drying (yellow, red, black).
beans.wetHulled.desc: Parchment is hulled while the beans are still wet. Typical of Gayo, Sumatra and Toraja.
beans.wetHulled.flavor: Earthy, spicy, heavy body, low acidity
beans.anaerobic.desc: Fermented in sealed tanks without oxygen before drying.
beans.note: For hot manual brews. Espresso stays around {esp}, and cold brew uses room-temperature water. Too sour? Go up 1–2°. Too bitter? Go down 1–2°.
